##### **//First Comment**

3 core screens. ⸻

**Cause & Effect Screen (What it does for the user)**

The Cause & Effect screen shows you **how the foods you eat actually impact your body**.

Instead of guessing, you’ll see:

What you ate  
How your body responded (bloating, energy, mood, etc.)  
When it happened

It connects the dots for you, like:  
👉 *Pizza → bloating (2 hrs later)*  
👉 *Salmon → better energy (next day)*

Over time, it highlights patterns and gives simple insights like:  
👉 *“Dairy is your biggest trigger.”*

*When a user says:*

*“I ate pizza”*

*“This protein bar messed me up”*

*Scans food 📷*

*👉 That **automatically becomes a log***

*No “add meal” button. No friction.*

***Then → Insights (Cause & Effect)***

*The app turns that into:*

*👉 Pizza → bloating (2 hrs later)*

*👉 Protein bar → low energy*

***Key principle (important)***

*❌ Don’t make users:*

*Log meals manually*

*Track calories*

*Fill forms*

*👉 That feels like work*

*⸻*

*✅ **Instead:***

*Make it feel like:*

*👉 “I’m just talking… but it’s learning me.”*

*🧠 **Where GutGood gets data (even without repeats) Insight** Macy Mind*

*You’re not just tracking “what they ate.”*

*You’re pulling from **4 data streams**:*

*⸻*

***1\.** 💬 **Chat (primary signal)***

*Even if they don’t log consistently, they still say things like:*

*“What should I eat for energy?”*  
*“Is this snack healthy?”*  
*“Why do I feel off?”*

*👉 That tells you:*

*their **goals***  
*their **problems***  
*what they’re **thinking about eating***

***Use it for:***

*“You’ve been asking a lot about energy…”*

*⸻*

***2\.** 📷 **Scanner (strongest fallback)***

*Even if they only scan randomly:*

*ingredients*  
*additives*  
*food type (processed vs whole)*

*👉 You can build insights like:*

*“Most foods you’ve scanned are highly processed…”*

*No repetition needed.*

*⸻*

***3\.** 🧠 **Ingredient Intelligence (this is BIG)***

*You already know:*

*seed oils*  
*added sugars*  
*preservatives*

*So even ONE scan gives value:*

*“This food contains additives linked to low energy and inflammation.”*

*👉 That becomes insight fuel.*

*⸻*

***4\.** 🧍 **Onboarding data (baseline)***

*You already asked:*

*goals*  
*sensitivities*  
*symptoms*

*👉 So even with low usage:*

*You can say:*

*“Since your goal is energy, foods high in refined carbs may be working against you.”*

*⸻*

*🔥 **THIS is the shift***

*You’re not saying:*

*“We need repeated logs”*

*You’re saying:*

*“We interpret behavior \+ inputs intelligently”*

*⸻*

*⚙️ **Insight Engine (simple logic)***

***If:***

*repeated foods \+ symptoms*  
   *👉 Pattern Insight (best)*

*⸻*

***Else if:***

*scans ≥ 2–3*  
   *👉 Ingredient Insight*

*⸻*

***Else if:***

*chat questions ≥ 2–3*  
   *👉 Behavioral Insight*

*⸻*

***Else:***

*👉 Goal-based Insight*

*⸻*

*💡 **Real examples (no repetition needed)***

***User scans 2 snacks:***

*“Both foods you scanned contain additives that can impact how your body feels—want cleaner options?”*

*⸻*

***User asks random health questions:***

*“You’ve been focusing on energy—what you eat daily plays a big role in that.”*

*⸻*

***User barely logs anything:***

*“Based on your goals, focusing on whole foods will help your body perform better.”*

*⸻*

*🧠 **Why this works***

*Most users:*

*won’t log perfectly*  
*won’t track daily*

*👉 But they WILL:*

*scan*  
*ask questions*  
*explore*

*That’s enough.*

*⸻*

*💸 **Cost advantage***

*These insights:*

*require **less data***  
*use **fewer AI calls***

*👉 cheaper than full pattern tracking*

*⸻*

*🔑 **Your system becomes:***

*Chat \+ Scans \+ Behavior → Insight Engine → Impact Screen*

*⸻*

*🧾 **Clean answer***

*👉 You collect data from:*

*chat behavior*  
*scans*  
*onboarding*  
*ingredient database*

*👉 You don’t rely on repeated food logs*

*👉 You generate insights based on **whatever signal exists***

##### **//Comment on 20/05/26**

The main idea is that GutGood is an AI food/body assistant.  
Core MVP should include:  
Chat screen  
Users can ask food, gut, craving, bloating, ingredient, and body reaction questions. They can also upload images or scan food.  
Food scanner  
The scanner should identify the food/product and show:  
score  
flagged ingredients  
how it may affect the user  
better swaps  
Insights screen  
This should show patterns from chat/scans, like foods that may trigger bloating, energy crashes, cravings, or sensitivity.  
Profile screen  
This should store user preferences, sensitivities, saved foods, goals, and personalization settings.  
Important: the app should not just give generic food suggestions. The goal is personalized food intelligence based on what the user asks, scans, and logs.

**For GutGood MVP**, these are the APIs/tools we should use:  
OpenAI API  
Purpose:  
AI chat responses  
image/photo analysis in chat  
ingredient explanations  
food/body reaction insights  
swap suggestions  
cycle sync style insights  
personalized wellness responses  
Open Food Facts API  
Purpose:  
barcode scanning  
product lookup  
ingredient lists  
nutrition facts  
packaged food data  
Supabase  
Purpose:  
backend/database  
user accounts  
chat history  
saved scans  
saved foods  
user preferences  
sensitivities  
insights/patterns  
App hosting/server  
Purpose:  
securely connect the app to OpenAI  
protect API keys  
handle requests between the app, database, and food API  
Core MVP flow:  
User types, uploads photo, or scans food → app checks food data → OpenAI explains the food/body impact → Supabase saves user patterns so GutGood feels personalized over time.  
**OpenAI \+ Open Food Facts \+ Supabase \+ secure backend/server.** 

##### **//More Details about Premium plans**

Just iOS … **GutGood want to offer users a 3-day free trial before the $4.99/month subscription starts.**

Free trial should allow users to:

chat with AI  
upload food photos  
scan products  
receive ingredient/body insights  
experience the core GutGood flow before subscribing.

**The $4.99/month premium plan unlocks the full GutGood experience.**  
Premium users get:  
unlimited AI chat  
unlimited food/photo scans  
ingredient breakdowns  
personalized food & body insights  
smarter food swaps  
saved food history/patterns  
cycle sync insights  
weekly gut recap insights  
deeper personalized answers over time as GutGood learns the user  
Free users can still try the app with limited chats/scans daily before upgrading. Free users can still experience the core GutGood app before upgrading.

Free version includes:

3–5 AI chats daily  
3 food/photo scans daily  
basic ingredient insights  
basic food swaps  
limited personalized wellness insights

Once users hit their daily limit, they will see the premium subscription screen.

This gives users enough access to understand the value of GutGood before subscribing to unlimited access.

The Body Pattern Engine is the backend feature that helps GutGood learn from each user over time.

OpenAI will help understand what the user ate, scanned, or typed. Then we save that structured data in Supabase.

The backend should compare patterns like:

foods eaten vs bloating  
protein before noon vs energy  
dairy/gluten vs symptoms  
sugar vs crashes  
caffeine timing vs sleep  
fiber vs stool/digestion

Then the app can show simple personalized insights like:

“Your energy seems higher on days you eat protein earlier.”

“Dairy appears often before your bloating logs.”

This should be framed as patterns, not medical diagnosis.

**Yes, Firebase can store the user data.**

**We can use Firebase for:**

**user accounts**  
**saved meals**  
**chat history**  
**symptoms/check-ins**  
**scan results**  
**pattern data**

**OpenAI would understand the food/chat, then Firebase stores the structured data. Our backend would use that saved data to find patterns over time.**

**Yes, that makes sense. We don’t need both Supabase and Firebase if Firebase can handle the data structure.**

**OpenAI understands the food/chat → Firebase stores the structured data → backend logic analyzes patterns → OpenAI explains those patterns to the user in simple language.**

##### **//Comment on 07/07/26**

Macy Mind Team, I want to discuss what I think could become one of GutGood’s biggest differentiators: **Smart Notifications powered by personal patterns.**

I don’t want generic reminders like “Log your meal” or “Drink water.” I want every notification to be earned by the user’s own data.

Examples:

“You’ve reported feeling more energized after eating breakfast before 9 AM.”

“The last 3 times you ate late, you reported lower energy the next morning.”

“Meals containing onions have been followed by bloating 4 out of your last 5 times.”

“No clear pattern yet. Keep logging so GutGood can learn what works for your body.”

The key principle is that **GutGood should speak in patterns, not absolutes.** We should never tell users that a specific food is “good” or “bad” for everyone. Instead, we show them what their own history suggests.

I’d like us to design a pattern engine that analyzes meal logs, food scans, ingredients, meal timing, symptoms, energy, mood, sleep, and other check-ins. Once we have enough data and confidence, the AI should generate personalized insights and trigger smart notifications at the right moments.

My vision is simple: **GutGood doesn’t nag users—it learns them.** That’s the experience I want us to build. I’d love everyone’s thoughts on the best architecture and approach for making this scalable. Team, to build smart notifications, we need four core pieces:

A structured data system that saves meal logs, food tags, ingredients, scan source, meal timing, symptoms, energy, mood, and sleep.

A pattern engine that detects repeated user-specific patterns, like bloating after certain ingredients or higher energy after certain meal times.

Confidence rules so GutGood does not show insights too early. We should only trigger insights after enough meals, check-ins, and repeat behavior.

A notification trigger system that sends insights at the right time, such as after a check-in, in a weekly report, or when the user scans/logs a food connected to their past symptoms.

The main principle: GutGood should not make absolute claims. It should say, “Your history shows…” or “You reported…” based on the user’s own data.

For Version 1, notifications should be sent based on simple rules:

**1\. Meal reminder**

Around the user’s selected breakfast, lunch, or dinner time (if they enabled reminders).

**2\. Post-meal check-in**

1–2 hours after a meal is logged.  
Example: “How are you feeling after your last meal?”

**3\. No meal logged**

If no meal has been logged by the evening (e.g., 7 PM), send:  
   “You haven’t logged a meal today. Take 30 seconds to check in.”

**4\. Daily reminder**

One reminder per day at the user’s preferred time if they haven’t opened the app.

Also allow users to:

Turn notifications on/off.  
Choose their reminder times.  
Choose which notifications they want to receive.

**Unsupported Topics Guardrail (MVP)**

GutGood should remain a **food intelligence app**, not a general AI assistant.

If the user’s message, photo, barcode, or scan is **not related to food or beverages**, do not attempt to answer it.

**Supported**

🍽 Meals  
🥤 Beverages  
📦 Food products  
📋 Food ingredient labels  
🍴 Restaurant menus  
🌿 Nutrition & gut health  
⚡ Food effects (energy, digestion, sleep, focus, etc.)

**Unsupported**

👟 Shoes  
👕 Clothing  
💄 Cosmetics & skincare  
🧴 Personal care  
🚗 Cars  
📱 Electronics  
🐶 Pets  
🎬 Movies & TV  
⚽ Sports  
📰 News  
💰 Finance  
💻 General knowledge  
Any non-food product

That’s outside what GutGood was built for. We exist to help you understand food—what’s in it, how it may affect your body, and how to make more informed choices.
